overview: Two ELISA formats used to detect antigen or antibody, differing in how many antibodies are used and how specific/sensitive the assay is.
genZNote: Direct ELISA: one antibody doing all the work. Sandwich ELISA: antigen gets squeezed between two.

aspects.label: Principle
aspects.valueA: Antigen is directly coated onto the plate and detected with a single labeled primary antibody.
aspects.valueB: A capture antibody is coated onto the plate, binds the antigen from the sample, and a second labeled detection antibody binds a different epitope on the same antigen.

aspects.label: Number of Antibodies Used
aspects.valueB: Two antibodies — an unlabeled capture antibody and a labeled detection antibody.

aspects.label: Specificity and Sensitivity
aspects.valueA: Lower specificity and sensitivity, since the antigen is not purified from the sample before detection.
aspects.valueB: Higher specificity and sensitivity, since the capture step selectively pulls the target antigen out of a complex sample.

aspects.label: Background Signal
aspects.valueA: Higher background/non-specific binding is more likely.
aspects.valueB: Lower background, due to the extra specificity from a second antibody.

aspects.label: Typical Use Case
aspects.valueA: Simple, rapid screening assays where high sensitivity is less critical.
aspects.valueB: Detecting low-abundance antigens in complex samples (e.g. serum, plasma) with high confidence.

aspects.label: Key Distinguishing Feature
aspects.valueA: Single antibody directly detects coated antigen.
aspects.valueB: Two antibodies capture and detect antigen, increasing specificity.
